questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university was of high standard, and that it was an interesting country where lots of people and cultures meet.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most but not all information was provided by UCPH. In general, this wasn't a problem.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much at all. We received information prior to going, but once we arrived, we had to figure most out ourselves.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it wasn't difficult, because I did my own research a long time before going.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It will most likely be very expensive for the quality you get.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university deadline for campus housing allocation is very late, and it is not made clear enough that very few students will actually receive campus accommodation. This leads students to believe that they will have a place to be once they arrive, but they will in fact have to find something on their own within a very short time.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You pick courses prior to going. Once you arrive, you book a time slot for vaccination registration and student card collection. This is very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email correspondence with the host.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get two thirds of the applied courses in the first round of application.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be careful with choosing high level courses. High level courses are a lot more difficult and require a lot more work at the host than at UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Expect a course to be more difficult at the host than if you would choose it at UCPH. Eg. a 3rd year course at the host would be similar to a 2nd year course at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A closer relationship to the lecturer. A bit more emphasis on assignments than lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Calculus for Computing
Introduction to Computational Biology
Optimisation Algorithms

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Optimisation Algorithms was a very exciting course but also difficult. Choose this if you are familiar with Kattis and have a strong profile in Algorithms and Data Structures. You should be proficient in C++. Be careful with choosing this course. It caught me by surprise how difficult it was.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Dining out is less expensive eg. canteens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of student clubs and you meet a lot of other people of different cultures in the classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking. There are a lot of cool places to hike eg. Sungei Buloh. Flights out are also cheap, which makes travel to nearby countries less expensive.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to other countries or explore the hiking opportunities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go and talk to whoever you think is interesting. Everyone is open minded and ready to go out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The laws within the country are strict. Public transportation within the country is not available at night.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture of Hawker centers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure you have your insurance in order.
Be careful when choosing courses. They are most likely more difficult than you think. At least for CS courses.
Find accommodation early on and don't rely on the host to find you housing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The things mentioned above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I met and friendships I have gotten. If you wish, you can form friendships with people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic part and the homesickness.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
